title: Majestic Corner
summary: Check the king onto a fork line, then sacrifice the rook to remove the defender of the promotion square.

nodes.question: How can White displace the rook from the h-file?
nodes.explanation: After ...Rh2, the rook stops h8=Q. A passive defense allows Black to create mating threats against Ka1.

nodes.question: Does defending the eighth rank change the idea?
nodes.explanation: After ...Rd8, Black stops h8=Q horizontally. White can rotate the same checking-fork idea onto the d-file.

branches.title: Check, fork, and clear the h-file
commentary: Begin after the source’s ...Rh2. The first saved image shows the h-pawn being dragged; the stable diagrams confirm it belongs on h7.
Rf1+ checks along the first rank. White first changes the black king’s square instead of passively defending h7.
Kd2 is the illustrated escape. The king now shares the second rank with Rh2.
Rf2+ checks the king and attacks Rh2. The rook offers itself to force the defender away from the h-file.
Rxf2 accepts the sacrifice, removing the checking rook but abandoning the promotion file.

h8=Q promotes safely. This exact queen-versus-rook position is winning for White; the lesson stops at the checked conversion rather than treating every queen-versus-rook position as automatically won.
branches.explanation: h8=Q promotes safely. This exact queen-versus-rook position is winning for White; the lesson stops at the checked conversion rather than treating every queen-versus-rook position as automatically won.

branches.title: Rotate the same fork onto the d-file
commentary: Compare the source’s other rook defense, ...Rd8, with the same kings and h7 pawn.
Rc6+ checks the king along the c-file, forcing it away from c1.
Kd2 is the illustrated move toward the center. The king now shares the d-file with Rd8.
Rd6+ checks and attacks the rook on d8 along one file. The geometry is the rotated version of Rf2+.
Rxd6 accepts the sacrifice and leaves the eighth rank unguarded.
h8=Q promotes. The exact resulting queen-versus-rook position is checked as a White win.
branches.explanation: h8=Q promotes. The exact resulting queen-versus-rook position is checked as a White win.

branches.title: Defend the pawn without checking
commentary: Compare the source’s passive rook lift, then correct its illustrated Black reply.
Rf7 protects h7 but gives away the win. Black can hold by keeping the rook on the h-file without stepping into a checking fork.
Kd2 threatens ...Rh1 mate but is an error: the king now shares the second rank with Rh2. White regains a forced win.
Rf2+ is an independently supplied correction to the source’s conclusion. White meets the mating threat with a checking fork of king and rook.
Rxf2 accepts the sacrifice and removes the checking rook, but releases the h-file.
h8=Q reaches a checked White win. Thus the source’s ...Kd2 does not demonstrate a forced draw, even though the earlier Rf7 really did give away the win.
branches.classification: independent alternative correcting an illustrated source reply with representative legal completion
branches.explanation: h8=Q reaches a checked White win. Thus the source’s ...Kd2 does not demonstrate a forced draw, even though the earlier Rf7 really did give away the win.

branches.title: Black keeps the rook on the h-file
commentary: This independent defense shows how Black really holds after the passive rook lift.
Rf7 gives away the win, but Black must avoid the checking fork created by ...Kd2.
Rh3 keeps the rook behind h7 and leaves the king on c1. The checking-fork setup is absent; this exact position is drawn with best play.
branches.classification: independent alternative with representative legal replies
branches.explanation: ...Rh3 keeps the rook on the promotion file without putting king and rook on a checking-fork line.

exercises.prompt: Why check before sacrificing the rook?
exercises.answer: The check places Black’s king on the same rank as its rook, allowing Rf2+ to attack both. A rook capture then releases the h-file.

exercises.prompt: What is the shared idea behind Rc6+ and Rf1+?
exercises.answer: Both checks move the king onto a line with its rook. The next checking fork either wins that rook or deflects it from h8.

startContext: Begin after the illustrated ...Rh2; reconstruct this position from the stable Rf7 diagram and the narrated rook move. A separate node shows the saved ...Rd8 defense. The initial transient h-pawn drag is not treated as a pawn on h6.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.

sourceCorrections.claim: After ...Rh2 Rf7, the illustrated ...Kd2 forces White to leave the corner and Black holds the draw.
sourceCorrections.correction: Rf7 does draw, but ...Kd2 gives White a win again: Rf2+ forks king and rook, then ...Rxf2 h8=Q wins. The independently checked ...Rh3 holds the draw instead. Queen versus rook is checked in the exact resulting positions, not assumed to be a universal win.
